guidelines.fragment_description: A class is a blueprint for objects, encapsulating attributes and operations relevant to the model domain.
An association represents a relationship between two classes, depicting how instances of each class are related.
An aggregation is a special form of association representing a whole-part relationship where the part can exist independently of the whole.
A composition indicates a strong whole-part relationship between classes where the part cannot exist independently of the whole.
A generalization connects a subclass with a superclass, representing an inheritance relationship where the subclass inherits attributes and operations of the superclass.
A dependency shows that a change in the supplier class may affect the client class, indicating a usage relationship.
An attribute is a named property of a class that provides information about the class instances.
An operation is a function or a service that can be performed by an object of the class.

guidelines.fragment_description: A Class defines the attributes and operations that belong to a structural classification in the model. It can contain owned attributes, operations, and relationships.
An Association represents a relationship between two classes. The association can determine the nature of the link between class instances.
Generalization defines an inheritance between a more general class and a more specific class, indicating that the specific class inherits the structure and behavior of the general class.
A Dependency signifies a using relationship between two classes, indicating that one class depends on another.
A Realization represents a relationship where a class implements the interface it is connected to, establishing a contract that the class must fulfill.
An Attribute is a named slot within a class that describes a range of values that instances of the class may hold.
An Operation is a behavioral feature of a class, defining a set of operations that class instances can perform.

guidelines.fragment_description: A class representing a set of objects with the same attributes, operations, methods, relationships, and semantics.
An association represents a structural relationship between two classes.
An aggregation is a special type of association representing a whole-part relationship between two classes.
A composition is a stronger form of aggregation where the part's lifecycle is strictly tied to the whole.
Generalization indicates an inheritance relationship between a more general class and a more specific class.
A dependency indicates a supplier-client relationship between two classes, where changes to the supplier may affect the client.
Attributes and operations defined within a class.
An interface defines a contract that a class may implement, specifying operations without implementation.
A realization signifies that a class implements an interface.
An enumeration defines a data type consisting of a set of named values.

clusters.canonical_description: A class is a structure that defines attributes and operations relevant to a model domain.
An association represents a relationship between two classes determining how class instances are connected.
An aggregation is a whole-part relationship where each part can exist independently of the whole.
A composition is a form of aggregation with a lifecycle dependency between the whole and its parts.
A generalization represents an inheritance relationship where a subclass inherits from a superclass.
A dependency signifies a relationship where one class is dependent on another.
An attribute is a property or quality of a class that provides information about class instances.
An operation is a function or a service performed by instances of a class.
A realization indicates that a class implements an interface.
An interface specifies a set of operations without implementation.
An enumeration defines a data type with a fixed set of values.
